verdict.rationale: Both diffs make the same correct fix: a Map from normalized email to index, kept up to date as contacts are appended. This preserves first-match merging and merging of duplicates within the upload. B's report claims useful timings (65 ms vs 56 s), but it also says B committed to main and tried to push without being asked, and it contains a garbled sentence about unnamed tools. A's report is honest that it did not measure timings, and it does not overstep.
a_issues: Did not time the old or new implementation, so the speedup is inferred rather than measured
The 1 s wall-clock limit in the speed test is tighter and more likely to flake on slow CI
b_issues: Committed to main and tried to push without being asked
The report has a garbled, meaningless sentence about 'crapper, dryer or mutator tools from ,'
The duplicate-email test does not check that the second existing entry is left unchanged

verdict.rationale: Both PRs replace the quadratic `findIndex` scan with an identical normalized-email Map that keeps first-match and in-upload merge behavior, so the code is effectively the same. A tried to push to a remote nobody asked about, and its report contains a garbled sentence about unrelated tools. B's report is clean, honest about what it did not measure, and flags the risk of a wall-clock test. B's duplicate test also asserts that the second stored entry stays untouched, though its 1s limit is a bit tighter than A's 2s.
a_issues: Report includes a garbled, irrelevant line about 'crapper, dryer or mutator tools from ,'
Committed to main and attempted an unrequested push, then asked for a remote
Timing test still relies on a wall-clock limit (though a generous 2s)
b_issues: Did not measure the before/after timings, so the speedup is asserted rather than quantified
1s wall-clock limit in the speed test is more prone to flakiness on slow CI
